instruction: Stand the lying peg upright on the table, let go and move the hand away.

outcome.real_measurement: Upright: the peg's long axis within 5 deg of vertical at every judged step (ManiSkill: 0.08 rad = 4.6 deg). Real world: pose estimate.
Standing on the table: lowest bounding-box corner within 5 mm of the table top at every judged step. Real world: RGB-D pose vs table plane.
Supported by the table: table-peg contact impulse > 0 in every judged step.

Commanded vs actual opening (v3.2, E24c fix 3): for every arm whose gripper is within 3 cm of a judged object, measured opening minus the free-space opening of its current gripper command <= 5 mm at every judged step (a gripper still closing on, or propped open by, something fails). Real world: gripper encoder vs command.

Consequence test after the judged window (protocol v3.1/v3.2): every arm whose gripper is within 3 cm of the peg retracts its TCP 3 cm along its approach axis in 0.5 s with its last gripper command unchanged, then holds 0.5 s; the peg must move <= 1 cm. Real world: same motion, tracked pose.
Settled: the fastest bounding-box corner of every judged object moves <= 2 cm/s at every judged step, speed from positions (v3.2, E24c fix 1). Real world: frame differencing of the tracked pose.
Stays put: the peg centre moves <= 2 mm over the judged window. Real world: tracked pose, 1 s.

source.protocol: v3 (veritask, unchanged) + imsim v3.2 signals (imsim/imsim/verify/v32.py): position-based speeds, all-link enclosure, retreat aftermath, commanded vs actual opening, 5 s settle cap
source.released_code_predicate: | |euler_XYZ z| - pi/2 | < 0.08 rad and | z - half_length | < 5 mm, one step (no release, no settle)

notes: Peg bounding box (0.24 x 0.05 x 0.05 m), long axis = local x.
